use commerce
# Two parties agree on terms. We propose them; the customer signs (in person
# above HKD 1,000,000) before the start date; we countersign, and the terms
# are effective until we close them with the customer's consent. Amendments
# need the customer's consent too, and only while the terms are proposed.
contract Agreement
parties we, customer

thing Terms
  terms text
  amount HKD
  starts date

can amend by we with new_amount HKD, new_start date
  requires proposed
  requires consent of customer
  requires new_amount > HKD 0
  if new_amount > amount * 150%
    reject "an amendment may raise the amount by half at most"
  otherwise
    amount = new_amount
  starts = new_start
can sign by customer
  over 1_000_000 requires in person
  requires now < starts
  proposed -> signed
can countersign by we
  signed -> effective
can close by we
  requires consent of customer
  effective -> closed

test "signed in person, countersigned, and closed"
  we create at 2026-10-14 with terms = "100 t of steel, monthly", amount = HKD 1_500_000, starts = 2027-01-01
  we amend with new_amount = HKD 2_000_000, new_start = 2027-01-08 -> proposed
  customer sign -> refused "bo:in-person sign"
  customer sign in person -> signed
  we amend with new_amount = HKD 1, new_start = 2027-01-08 -> refused "bo:requires amend 1"
  we countersign -> effective
  we close at 2027-06-30 -> closed
  we close -> refused

test "what one party cannot do alone"
  we create with terms = "100 t of steel, monthly", amount = HKD 500_000, starts = 2027-01-01
  we amend with new_amount = HKD 600_000, new_start = 2027-01-01 -> consent of customer
  we amend with new_amount = HKD 900_000, new_start = 2027-01-01
  -> refused "an amendment may raise the amount by half at most"
  we sign -> consent of customer
  customer countersign -> refused "bo:state countersign"
  customer sign by AI agent -> signed
  customer countersign -> consent of we
  we close -> refused "bo:state close"

test "too late to sign"
  we create with terms = "100 t of steel, monthly", amount = HKD 500_000, starts = 2027-01-01
  customer sign at 2027-01-02 -> refused "bo:requires sign 2"

# A core enterprise's receivable, split down its supply chain (multi-tier
# supply-chain finance). The core enterprise (the issuer) owes its tier-1
# supplier and pays at maturity. The supplier splits the receivable among its
# own suppliers, who may split their parts again: each part is an instance of
# its own, backed by the same promise to pay, which its holder can keep, sell,
# or pledge to a bank for financing. The core enterprise's ledger keeps every
# part; each holder consents on its own ledger.
use finance
contract MultiTierReceivable
parties issuer, supplier

asset Receivable
  amount CNY
  due date
  tier number
  holder supplier

# Splitting is the standard library's split: the holder starts it, every
# recipient consents, the parts add up to the amount, and each part is one
# tier down. The alliance's own rule: parts go down to tier 5.
can split
  requires tier < 5
can transfer
can pledge
  over 5_000_000 requires in person
can release
can pay
can confirm payment
when due issuer pays

# Its tests: bo test runs each on an instance of its own, as the ledger
# would. A step acts on the part its party holds (or is pledgee or payee
# of); `issuer pay forge` pays the part the forge holds.
test "split across three tiers, financed by a bank, paid at maturity"
  issuer issue with amount = CNY 1_000_000, due = 2027-06-30, tier = 1
  supplier split with parts = (CNY 600_000, CNY 400_000), recipients = (gears, castings) -> divided
  gears split with parts = (CNY 250_000, CNY 350_000), recipients = (forge, gears) -> divided
  forge pledge to bank1 -> pledged
  issuer pay forge at 2027-06-30 -> paid
  bank1 confirm payment -> settled
  issuer pay gears -> paid
  gears confirm payment -> settled
  issuer pay castings -> paid
  castings confirm payment -> settled

test "every recipient consents, and only the holder splits"
  issuer issue with amount = CNY 1_000_000, due = 2027-06-30, tier = 1
  supplier split with parts = (CNY 600_000, CNY 400_000), recipients = (gears, castings) -> consent of castings
  gears split with parts = CNY 1_000_000, recipients = gears -> consent of supplier

test "the parts add up to the amount"
  issuer issue with amount = CNY 1_000_000, due = 2027-06-30, tier = 1
  supplier split with parts = (CNY 600_000, CNY 300_000), recipients = (gears, castings) -> refused "bo:requires split 5"

test "parts go down to tier 5"
  issuer issue with amount = CNY 1_000_000, due = 2027-06-30, tier = 4
  supplier split with parts = CNY 1_000_000, recipients = gears -> divided
  gears split with parts = CNY 1_000_000, recipients = forge -> refused "bo:requires split 1"

test "a pledged part neither splits nor moves"
  issuer issue with amount = CNY 1_000_000, due = 2027-06-30, tier = 1
  supplier split with parts = (CNY 600_000, CNY 400_000), recipients = (gears, castings)
  gears pledge to bank1 -> pledged
  gears split with parts = CNY 600_000, recipients = forge -> refused "bo:state split"
  gears transfer to forge -> refused "bo:state transfer"

# A core enterprise's receivable, split down its supply chain (multi-tier
# supply-chain finance). The core enterprise (the issuer) owes its tier-1
# supplier and pays at maturity. The supplier splits the receivable among its
# own suppliers, who may split their parts again: each part is an instance of
# its own, backed by the same promise to pay, which its holder can keep, sell,
# or pledge to a bank for financing. The core enterprise's ledger keeps every
# part; each holder consents on its own ledger.
use finance
contract MultiTierReceivable
parties issuer, supplier

asset Receivable
  amount CNY
  due date
  tier number
  holder supplier

# Splitting is the standard library's split: the holder starts it, every
# recipient consents, the parts add up to the amount, and each part is one
# tier down. The alliance's own rule: parts go down to tier 5.
can split
  requires tier < 5
can transfer
can pledge
  over 5_000_000 requires in person
can release
can pay
can confirm payment
when due issuer pays

# Its tests: bo test runs each on an instance of its own, as the ledger
# would. A step acts on the part its party holds (or is pledgee or payee
# of); `issuer pay forge` pays the part the forge holds.
test "split across three tiers, financed by a bank, paid at maturity"
  issuer issue with amount = CNY 1_000_000, due = 2027-06-30, tier = 1
  supplier split with parts = (CNY 600_000, CNY 400_000), recipients = (gears, castings) -> divided
  gears split with parts = (CNY 250_000, CNY 350_000), recipients = (forge, gears) -> divided
  forge pledge to bank1 -> pledged
  issuer pay forge at 2027-06-30 -> paid
  bank1 confirm payment -> settled
  issuer pay gears -> paid
  gears confirm payment -> settled
  issuer pay castings -> paid
  castings confirm payment -> settled

test "every recipient consents, and only the holder splits"
  issuer issue with amount = CNY 1_000_000, due = 2027-06-30, tier = 1
  supplier split with parts = (CNY 600_000, CNY 400_000), recipients = (gears, castings) -> consent of castings
  gears split with parts = CNY 1_000_000, recipients = gears -> consent of supplier

test "the parts add up to the amount"
  issuer issue with amount = CNY 1_000_000, due = 2027-06-30, tier = 1
  supplier split with parts = (CNY 600_000, CNY 300_000), recipients = (gears, castings) -> refused "bo:requires split 5"

test "parts go down to tier 5"
  issuer issue with amount = CNY 1_000_000, due = 2027-06-30, tier = 4
  supplier split with parts = CNY 1_000_000, recipients = gears -> divided
  gears split with parts = CNY 1_000_000, recipients = forge -> refused "bo:requires split 1"

test "a pledged part neither splits nor moves"
